newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes quiet as July market fizzles out.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes quiet as July market fizzles out.

text.p: North Sea physical and paper crude markets saw little action on Tuesday morning, with August loading schedules failing to surprise traders.
The August Brent programme was set at the equivalent of 38.5 cargoes of 500,000 barrels each, down three from July.
But the lower volumes were more than balanced by a fatter Forties programme which scheduled nearly seven more cargoes.
"The programmes are basically in line with expectations," said one trader.
The July market was seen going out with a whimper. No wet cargoes were heard offered in the morning.
Buyers too stuck to the sidelines despite a recent improvement in refining margins.
"It's very quiet this morning," said one trader. "Buyers are very relaxed...Refining margins are okay but not fantastic."
Traders assessed Dated Brent at August -20/-15 cents, in line with Monday's trade. Two late July cargoes also changed hands late on Monday at quotes-related levels.
The first cargoes from the August Brent programme are due to turn wet on Thursday.
Outright prices recovered slightly from Monday, trading eight cents up at $17.90 a barrel on the IPE at 1235 GMT.
Intermonth spreads were also slightly firmer, but were untraded. August/September was bid at -8 cents, and September/October talked at -15/-13 cents.
CFDs for next week (July 21-25) traded twice at September Brent -23 cents, with this week (July 15-18) three cents in backwardation.
